chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Mis'mam said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who forgot to shave his head or shorten [his hair] until he departed [from Mina]. He said: He should shave [or shorten] on the road or wherever he is, and this does not contradict the first two reports, because this narration is applied to one who is unable to return to Mina. As for one who is able to return, it is necessary to do so according to what we have previously mentioned. And with that, if he is unable to return, he should bring his hair back to Mina and bury it there, which indicates that.

key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, a holy site near Mecca central to Hajj rituals
key_terms.نَفَرَ: To depart (specifically from Mina after prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who forgets to shave his head before departing Mina?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records Imam al-Sadiq’s (AS) clarification that the obligation to shave or shorten hair applies wherever the pilgrim is if they forgot before departing Mina, provided they cannot easily return. This ruling harmonizes with earlier reports by distinguishing between those unable to return to Mina and those who are, ensuring the ritual completion of Hajj is not neglected due to forgetfulness. The hadith underscores the Shia scholarly principle of reconciling apparent contradictions in narrations through contextual application (*ta'wil*).
